messages.author: e715a3aeb27b07f3
messages.subject: plyr with R2.14 on Mac
parts:
Hi there,

I used 'plyr' in the past without any problems but since I did the
update to R 2.14 I cannot load the package anymore. Even after a fresh
installation of the package:

> library(plyr)
Error in get(Info[i, 1], envir = env) :
internal error -3 in R_decompress1
Error: package/namespace load failed for ‘plyr’

Any idea what could have went wrong?

That's what I was thinking, so to get around it I just downloaded the sources from CRAN (with extensions .tar.gz instead of .tgz).  Since plyr depends on itertools and iterators, I tried installing those from inside R; but R conks on iterators just like on plyr. 

But there's a difference.  When you download the sources and try to install them from the terminal, iterators and itertools go through, but not plyr :

messages.author: 7e921b60a6dff156
messages.subject: Re: plyr with R2.14 on Mac
parts:
Hi,

With some quote pruning:

On Mon, Nov 7, 2011 at 11:36 AM, David Kahle <david...@gmail.com> wrote:
[snip]

> David-Kahle:Downloads david_kahle$ R CMD install plyr_1.6.tar.gz
> * installing to library
> ‘/Library/Frameworks/R.framework/Versions/2.14/Resources/library’
> * installing *source* package ‘plyr’ ...
> ** libs
> *** arch - i386
> sh: make: command not found
> ERROR: compilation failed for package ‘plyr’
> * removing
> ‘/Library/Frameworks/R.framework/Versions/2.14/Resources/library/plyr’
> Does that make any sense to you?  Is the real problem with iterators, and
> plyr is just piggy-backing on a different problem?

This problem is that you do not have a gcc toolchain installed on your
system. You can easily remedy this by installing XCode for your system
(the latest one for your OS is always best, but otherwise you can
install the one from the Developer's DVD that came w/ your OS X
install).

An alternative (I think) would be to download the mac binary packages
from their CRAN pages and install them that way ... but, you should
have gcc installed anyway, so go ahead and install XCode ;-)

-steve
--
Steve Lianoglou

 | Weill Medical College of Cornell University

> Speaking of R and > sh: make: command not found I did have an issue with my recent install of R and Lion.

No, it was not there.

> Turned out the problem was that R was looking for gcc in the wrong place and once I linked it
>
> sudo ln -s /usr/bin/gcc /usr/bin/gcc-4.2
> sudo ln -s /usr/bin/g++ /usr/bin/g++-4.2
>

It's a bit dangerous hack since gcc itself is a symlink so a) you're linking the wrong thing and b) you can cause inifinite loops (e.g. if 4.2 will be selected).

My recommendation would be to install Xcode 4.1 first (or just gcc-4.2 if you want), because the above will fix only some parts, other things like gfortran won't work (you're missing a lot of the gcc-4.2 pieces). But if you really don't want to do that, you may want to use

sudo ln -s llvm-gcc-4.2 /usr/bin/gcc-4.2
sudo ln -s llvm-g++-4.2 /usr/bin/g++-4.2

to re-direct gcc-4.2 to the llvm version.

> it worked fine. If you have Xcode installed, make sure that R knows where to look. Previously I've not had this issue and I wonder if it's because Apple is changing things on Simon.
>

Well, you didn't include the details, but my guess would be that you have installed Xcode 4.2 on a clean Lion installation (read: you didn't install Xcode 4.1). On Lion Xcode contains three compilers: gcc-4.2, llvm-gcc-4.2 and clang. With Lion, Apple has switched the default to gcc-llvm (and they plan to phase that out, too), that's why CRAN R binary uses gcc-4.2 explicitly, because that's what is used to compile it. Now apparently what Apple did is to remove gcc-4.2 from Xcode 4.2 (it's still there in Xcode 4.1).

> I suppose if others have the issue, maybe this will help...
>

Hopefully the update makes clear what's happening and what are the correct options.

No, it was not there.


Turned out the problem was that R was looking for gcc in the wrong place and once I linked it

sudo ln -s /usr/bin/gcc /usr/bin/gcc-4.2
sudo ln -s /usr/bin/g++ /usr/bin/g++-4.2


It's a bit dangerous hack since gcc itself is a symlink so a) you're linking the wrong thing and b) you can cause inifinite loops (e.g. if 4.2 will be selected).

My recommendation would be to install Xcode 4.1 first (or just gcc-4.2 if you want), because the above will fix only some parts, other things like gfortran won't work (you're missing a lot of the gcc-4.2 pieces). But if you really don't want to do that, you may want to use

sudo ln -s llvm-gcc-4.2 /usr/bin/gcc-4.2
sudo ln -s llvm-g++-4.2 /usr/bin/g++-4.2

to re-direct gcc-4.2 to the llvm version.


it worked fine. If you have Xcode installed, make sure that R knows where to look. Previously I've not had this issue and I wonder if it's because Apple is changing things on Simon.


Well, you didn't include the details, but my guess would be that you have installed Xcode 4.2 on a clean Lion installation (read: you didn't install Xcode 4.1). On Lion Xcode contains three compilers: gcc-4.2, llvm-gcc-4.2 and clang. With Lion, Apple has switched the default to gcc-llvm (and they plan to phase that out, too), that's why CRAN R binary uses gcc-4.2 explicitly, because that's what is used to compile it. Now apparently what Apple did is to remove gcc-4.2 from Xcode 4.2 (it's still there in Xcode 4.1).
